lines: I marked where the raiders came through. I also marked where you turned them back.
Maps make borders look calm. You reminded me borders have to be defended.
I can point to where you met them. That spot feels different now.
A village border is not ink. Yesterday, you made that clear.
You changed the shape of the danger before it reached the center.
I marked the raid path. I also marked where it stopped.
The map of this place has one more reason to keep its name.
You made the distance between <red><bold>raiders</bold></red> and homes matter.
We moved supplies away from the outer walls before the fighting started.
I learned which doorway gives the clearest view of the square.
I have marked two fallback routes from the square to the safest houses.
The northern hedge blocks our view long before it blocks an attacker.
A cart left in the wrong lane can ruin the cleanest retreat plan.
The bell should be audible from every field path, not only the center.
I want distance markers on the outer road so warnings arrive with numbers.
The well sits in open ground. We need cover near it before the next siege.
Children should know one route to shelter that never crosses the main gate.
The west wall needs a lookout who can see past the bend in the river.
I keep a simple defense chart where shaking hands can still read it.
After every attack, I redraw the village from the raider's point of view.
